items.title: Jerry Hey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 2, 2023
items.q: even if you’re Celine Dion or Whitney Houston or anything, it’s David is in charge there.

ctx.x: Quincy is all about personality. You just, when you go into the studio with him you feel like the record would fail if you weren’t in on this session. That’s how he makes you feel, that you are a major part of this record-making process. And it’s family, it’s — you have a good time, you play great music, great engineer, great songs. He always works with the best artists. You know how can it not be great? That’s Quincy’s thing. I mean plus he picks songs you know. He always says the song comes first and yes it…

that he was playing on with Abraham Laboriel, bass; Lukather on guitar; I believe it was Steve Gadd on drums; and Jay Graydon, the producer/guitar player also, didn’t like the bridge. So Jay said, “David, I don’t really like the bridge you know, let’s work on the bridge.” So with they’re all — including me — standing around the piano with David Foster and he goes [scats] how’s that? And it was like, wow that was ridiculous. I mean this was just like cold doing this. And David goes, “Na, try something else.” And…
And I wouldn’t have thought of that, right.
